transcript.text: The supply cart stops at the edge of the trees. Larkhaven: a handful of roofs and a ranch fence that runs right up to the forest.
Everything here looks faded, like an old picture left in the sun. You too.
There you are! You must be the new tamer. I'm Maren. I keep the ranch.
Before anything else: the ranch register. Every tamer in the valley signs it. Write yourself in, love.
As the ink dries, colour runs into you: your hands, your clothes, your hair. You're the only bright thing on the road.
Rowan. Good name. And look at you, bright as a new penny!
Don't mind the rest of it. The whole valley faded long ago. Like an old photo, isn't it?
Larkhaven farmfolk, it says here. A farm family! Then you know how to look after things that can't tell you what's wrong.
Your grandmother always said the land grew tired. People took and took from it, and one hard winter it simply let its colour go. "Look after the land," she'd say, "and one day it'll remember."
Every family in this valley tells it a little differently. I once heard four tellings at one harvest supper. They can't all be right. Maybe they can't all be wrong, either.
Folk say it comes back, a little, every time someone earns a creature's trust. Come to the barn. Someone's been waiting for you.
Here they are. Three young ones, born this spring, and every one of them hoping for a tamer.
Go and say hello. Take your time, love; this is the big one. They'll be choosing you as much as you choose them.
You kneel in the straw. Cindercub looks at you for a long moment, then steps forward and presses its head into your hand.
Colour floods out from it: gold straw, red beams, a blue sky in the high window.
...There. It chose you right back. And the world remembered a little.
Nobody owns a creature, love; they choose. The other two will find their tamers. Wren's due by later, and that one never could wait.
Off you go, then. Show Cindercub the valley.
